0a398a396db115: Numbers, patterns and proofs: the language the universe is written in.
01368e77afaf62: Euclid's Elements organized all of geometry from just five postulates and was used as a textbook for more than 2000 years. It's the best example of how solid knowledge is built: start from a few ideas and prove everything else.
0b98a70e7e29a7: Euclid demanded proof for everything. What claim you take for granted would you like to be able to prove? What steps would you use?
0322db13aad087: Draw any triangle with a ruler, measure its three angles and add them up. Repeat with a different triangle.
16891631c0c368: The Pythagorean theorem says that in a right triangle a² + b² = c². The Babylonians already knew triples like 3-4-5 more than a thousand years earlier: Pythagoras (or his school) is famous for the idea of proving it, not just using it.
1456fe6e9e5a5f: If a right triangle has legs of 5 and 12, how long is the hypotenuse? Explain how you calculated it.
1963053b15cc8b: Find a right angle in your house (a corner) and check with a piece of string that 3-4-5 forms it.
0f6ed2057751d0: Archimedes bounded the value of π between 223/71 and 22/7 using 96-sided polygons inside and outside a circle. Without calculators or decimals, he got three correct digits more than 2200 years ago.
0cde5dcd7ebe6b: Why do you think π is the same for any circle, big or small?
019815104ce4c8: Measure the rim and the diameter of a lid or a cup, divide rim ÷ diameter, and note how close it comes to 3.14.
0df4f6f55fe379: In his book Liber Abaci (1202), Fibonacci introduced the Hindu-Arabic numerals (0–9) we use today to Europe. It also features the sequence 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8… arising from a problem about rabbit reproduction.
1a75bffa46d2ab: Write the next 5 numbers of the sequence 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8… and explain the rule.
0281c4f74ec7ea: Look in nature (flowers, pinecones, shells) for something you can count in Fibonacci numbers.
16ec18bf7e27ab: Emmy Noether proved that every symmetry in nature corresponds to a conservation law (for example, energy is conserved because the laws don't change over time). Einstein called her a creative mathematical genius.
18680839ec51e5: What does it mean for something to have "symmetry"? Give an everyday example and a mathematical one.
0e2de72d270745: Fold a sheet of paper and cut out a symmetric shape. How many axes of symmetry does it have?
1c85f7a541d4a3: The word "algebra" comes from the title of a book by al-Khwarizmi, Al-jabr. And his own name, Latinized, gave rise to the word "algorithm": a list of steps for solving a problem.
05d6e009c53553: Write an algorithm (numbered steps) for someone to add two three-digit numbers by hand.
1e0c530caba56d: Solve: "I'm thinking of a number, I add 7 and get 20." What was it? Write the equation.
025f8d5aabbefc: Srinivasa Ramanujan taught himself math almost entirely on his own in India, and in 1913 wrote to G. H. Hardy at Cambridge with astonishing formulas. His series for calculating π are still used in computers today.
195fcdc1eb799c: What does Ramanujan's story teach you about learning without having every resource?
03282124786347: Pick a hard problem you left unfinished this week and try it once more, without asking for help, for 15 minutes.
1ae32c627d53ba: The big questions: what is just, what is true, and what makes a good life.
10891c8753fc9b: Socrates never wrote a single book: he did philosophy by talking in the public squares of Athens. His method was to ask questions until the other person discovered for themselves that they didn't know what they thought they knew. He was sentenced to death in 399 BC and chose to drink hemlock rather than give up philosophizing.
15d9651d585844: Socrates said "all I know is that I know nothing." What's something you think you know for certain, and how could you check that it's true?
042f1a5f12feef: Pick a belief of yours and ask yourself "why?" five times in a row. Write down how far you get.
00359aeb093c66: Plato founded the Academy in Athens around 387 BC, considered the first institution of higher learning in the West. In The Republic he tells the allegory of the cave: people in chains who mistake the shadows on a wall for reality.
0007041c141bd3: In the allegory of the cave, what "shadows" do people today mistake for reality (social media, ads, rumors)?
19e1bec7939abc: For a while today, notice how many things you see or read are made to grab your attention, not to inform you.
0065dffb3bd353: Aristotle studied for 20 years at the Academy and was Alexander the Great's teacher. He invented formal logic (the syllogism) and argued that happiness (eudaimonia) is achieved by practicing virtues, seeking the "golden mean" between excess and deficiency.
0b03ee832de782: Courage is the middle ground between cowardice and recklessness. Pick another virtue and describe its two extremes.
1e9d3f477df887: Practice a small virtue today (patience, tidiness, generosity) and write down how it went by the end of the day.
19c2ae5150593a: Marcus Aurelius was a Roman emperor and a Stoic. He wrote his Meditations as a journal to himself. The central idea of Stoicism: distinguish what depends on us (our judgments and actions) from what doesn't (what others do, the weather, the past).
1a7b13878d0a7d: Make two lists: which things in your life depend on you and which don't. Which ones do you spend more energy on?
12e8a1a84d870b: Today, when something bothers you, ask yourself: "does this depend on me?" If not, let it go and write down what happened.
0ce1660d035182: René Descartes decided to doubt everything that could be doubted in order to find a solid foundation. He concluded he couldn't doubt that he was thinking: "I think, therefore I am" (cogito, ergo sum). With this he launched modern philosophy.
1ea4dcbcb9b967: Can you be sure you're not dreaming right now? What would make you doubt it, or not?
11e3cdfb5fa951: Apply methodical doubt to a rumor or a news story today: what evidence backs it up?
0af5f27fa630a6: Immanuel Kant proposed the categorical imperative: act only according to a rule you would want everyone to follow. For him, "Sapere aude" (dare to think for yourself) summed up the Enlightenment. He lived his whole life in Königsberg, with such an exact routine that neighbors set their clocks by him.
1306b3eb36416c: Is it okay to make an exception "just this once"? Apply the categorical imperative to a specific case.
1c35c7d173e008: Before a decision today, ask yourself: "what if everyone did the same thing?" Write down the answer.
0b2da914fa265a: Simone de Beauvoir, a French existentialist philosopher, wrote The Second Sex (1949), arguing that "one is not born, but rather becomes, a woman" — meaning many roles are socially constructed. For existentialism, each person is responsible for giving their own life meaning.
198c2c9df195de: What "roles" has society assigned you that you'd choose to consciously change or keep?
0386e4d487c7c7: Write five lines: "a decision I made this week that was truly mine."
136ece599d6ae8: Understanding where we come from to decide where we're going.
05f8e77bd4b969: The word "history" comes from the Greek historía, meaning inquiry. Herodotus traveled through Egypt, Persia and Greece asking questions and comparing versions to write his Histories, about the wars between Greeks and Persians. That's why he's called "the father of history."
0ff902989a7773: Herodotus investigated by asking multiple witnesses. Why is it useful to hear more than one version of the same event?
149498a25f775c: Ask two different people to tell you about the same family memory and note what matches and what doesn't.
0a6ccf89b5b125: Ibn Khaldun was a North African thinker who wrote the Muqaddimah, an introduction to history. He proposed explaining events through social and economic causes, not just what kings and battles did, anticipating sociology by centuries.
17ab8648b0729d: Pick a major historical change (a war, an invention). What underlying causes were there besides "one person's decision"?
0be1fc4f3a82e0: Write a timeline of 5 events on the same topic, noting what caused each one.
039c4ec32714ba: Cleopatra VII was the last active ruler of Ptolemaic Egypt. According to the historian Plutarch, she spoke several languages and was the first of her dynasty to learn Egyptian. She ruled at a time when Rome was expanding across the Mediterranean.
14910a949763e8: Cleopatra used languages and alliances to hold onto her kingdom. What "tools" do small countries use today to defend themselves?
19c3bcf57df901: Look at a map for where Ptolemaic Egypt was and what territories Rome controlled at that time.
14b02f7a21cf6b: Leopold von Ranke pushed for history to be written from archival documents (primary sources) rather than just other books. His goal was to tell the past "as it actually happened," which gave rise to the modern historical method.
1decc1007c0ee0: Explain in your own words the difference between a primary and a secondary source, with an example of each.
0ed4361c2aa458: Find a primary source at home (a letter, an old photo, a document) and note what it tells you and what it doesn't.
10b78fb0809eec: Around 1450, Johannes Gutenberg developed the movable-type printing press in Mainz, Europe. Making books stopped being years of work for copyists: costs dropped, reading increased and ideas spread much faster.
001e3bd27fc4fb: What invention today do you think will change life as much as the printing press did? Why?
09adb13a048b19: Ask an older person what everyday object today didn't exist when they were young.
15586ec95bf201: Benito Juárez, born in Guelatao, Oaxaca, became president of Mexico. With the Reform Laws he separated Church and State and defended the country's sovereignty during the French intervention. He's remembered for the phrase "among individuals, as among nations, respect for the rights of others is peace."
021ce7abd28cf9: What does "respect for the rights of others" mean to you? Give an example from your daily life.
100dacae38265c: Find out if there's a street, school or plaza near you named after a historical figure, and why.
0c60b0357c8460: Nelson Mandela spent 27 years in prison for opposing apartheid, South Africa's system of racial segregation. He was released in 1990 and in 1994 became the first president elected in elections open to all races. He pushed for reconciliation instead of revenge.
14ba9ec22d76d6: Why do you think Mandela chose reconciliation instead of revenge? Would you have done the same?
1573d9cbbb1729: Write three lessons from history that you think we still need to learn today.
1e2ca9d888b8ec: Protect your identity, your accounts and your data.
09f224589bb007: Bruce Schneier, a cryptography expert, sums it up: "security is a process, not a product." A long password (a phrase with several words) is harder to guess than a short one with symbols, and should never be reused across accounts.
1e851fb33509bc: Why is a long phrase with several unrelated words more secure than a short word with a symbol?
11e2c0a05abf8f: Create a 4-word passphrase with unrelated words and change it on an important account (don't share it).
0677de17939827: Kevin Mitnick was a famous hacker who later became a security consultant. He explained that the weakest point usually isn't the machine but the person: social engineering tricks someone into handing over data, for example with an urgent message that looks like it's from a bank.
16db587b6b0cb1: Name three signs that a message might be phishing (urgency, odd links, a strange sender…).
0189cec5c1907e: Check your spam folder and pick one email: what gives it away as fake?
1bcb9f01e47c33: In 1976, Whitfield Diffie and Martin Hellman proposed public-key cryptography: you can encrypt with a key everyone knows and decrypt only with another key you keep to yourself. That idea gave us secure connections (the padlock in your browser) and digital signatures.
12e6011afb7e2b: Explain in your own words why turning on two-factor verification protects your account even if someone steals your password.
0d49da8aeb38b2: Turn on two-factor verification on an important account (email or social media).
132d43eaa0f7d5: Phil Zimmermann published PGP in 1991, a program that let anyone encrypt their emails. He argued that privacy is a right: if everything you write can be read, what gets limited is your freedom to express yourself.
1db13e942583ac: What information about yourself would you not want just anyone to see? Who has access to it today?
012b6e5728ddc2: Open an app's permissions (location, camera, microphone) and remove the ones it doesn't need.
0a4c6f7f1f9fd5: Vint Cerf and Bob Kahn designed the TCP/IP protocol in the 1970s, the foundation of the Internet. It was designed to connect networks, not to protect them — that's why security has been added on afterward with encryption, firewalls and other layers.
160d89252daf6a: Why is it dangerous to connect to a public WiFi network without any precautions?
193493eb965993: Check that the sites you use most start with https:// (the padlock).
0db52be1d3bf65: Alan Turing led the effort at Bletchley Park to break the German army's Enigma machine during World War II. It's estimated that cracking those messages shortened the war. It was one of the first great battles of cryptography.
0a65e308d036fa: Enigma's encrypted messages were partly broken because patterns repeated. What pattern of yours (passwords, habits) could be predictable?
13c76c70506dd9: Back up an important file in two different places (cloud and USB, for example).
1fca7ff093a904: Kerckhoffs's principle (1883) says an encryption system should remain secure even if the enemy knows everything about it except the key. That's why serious algorithms are public and tested by many experts: the only secret is the key.
177098529b6e7b: Why do you think a system whose workings are public is more trustworthy than a "secret" one?
03c8259d8c6485: Teach a family member a security rule and ask them to explain it back to you.
059ba611fda07a: Learn to work WITH AI: asking better, verifying and creating.
1f9399943d6f95: In 1950, Alan Turing asked "can machines think?" and proposed what's known as the Turing test: if a person talks with a machine and can't tell whether it's human, can we say it thinks? Today's AI assistants bring that question closer to home, and learning to ask them well (giving role, context and format) greatly improves the answers.
0957fac0810d57: Rewrite a vague question ("tell me about the Revolution") so an AI answers better: add role, task and format.
115a1a2c91aabd: Ask an AI the same question two ways (vague and detailed) and compare the answers.
10cd57ad56fc09: John McCarthy coined the term "artificial intelligence" in 1955 and organized the Dartmouth workshop in 1956, considered the birth of the field. Current models can "hallucinate": confidently making up facts. That's why you need to verify.
128dc3375c868b: Why can an AI give a wrong answer in a confident tone? How would you check it?
1737bbb130ffc0: Ask an AI for a fact (a date or a quote) and check it against a reliable source. Note whether it matched.
0008c205411ef3: Ada Lovelace wrote notes in 1843 on Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine, considered the first program in history. She already sensed a machine could manipulate symbols, not just numbers… but she also made clear it couldn't "create" anything on its own.
10a6be883cf80a: What repetitive task in your day could you hand off to a tool, and which would you rather keep doing yourself?
11768929882919: Write out the steps of a task you repeat every week, as if you were explaining it to a robot.
09b442cdbc72b5: Joy Buolamwini discovered that some facial recognition systems performed much worse on darker-skinned faces and on women. Her research "Gender Shades" (2018) showed how biased training data produces unfair results, and she founded the Algorithmic Justice League.
0b4f3ecd0c789a: When should you NOT use AI for a task (school, personal or work)? Give two reasons.
0675ec1cf88279: Write a personal rule for using AI honestly in your work.
01da58b66b9a76: Geoffrey Hinton was one of the pioneers of neural networks, systems that learn patterns from examples. He received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2024, along with John Hopfield, for this work. An AI doesn't "copy and paste": it adjusts millions of connections until it finds patterns.
175e7c382c20f6: Ask an AI for a poem about your city and edit it until it sounds like you. What did you change and why?
1aa00069fa7d4d: Write your final version of the poem and note which part is yours and which came from the AI.
02b9a60f1a64c2: Fei-Fei Li drove the creation of ImageNet (2009), a huge database of labeled images that made training modern computer vision models possible. No good data, no good AI: if a model is only shown certain kinds of images, it will fail on the rest.
1e491325a0cbca: Find something an AI answers badly or doesn't know. Why do you think it fails there?
17f4db290422e2: Test an AI with a question about something very local (your neighborhood, your school) and note what it gets right and what it makes up.
0840763deb3f89: Demis Hassabis founded DeepMind, whose AlphaGo system beat Lee Sedol, one of the world's best Go players, in 2016, and whose AlphaFold predicted protein structures — work that earned him the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2024 along with John Jumper and David Baker.
08db15d2b60589: Explain in your own words what a language model is, as if telling a friend who's never used one.
1cd06e5c192fb3: Write down three things you learned this week about using AI responsibly.
0277941969130d: The human body, health and how to take care of them.
183ffe60348822: In 1543, Andreas Vesalius published De humani corporis fabrica, a book with very precise drawings of the body made from dissections. He corrected errors that had been repeated since antiquity and helped found modern anatomy.
180bfdf0729439: Name five bones in the body and say where they are. Which one do you think is most important, and why?
09555f9466a224: Locate 5 bones on your own body (skull, collarbone, femur, ribs, kneecap…) and touch them.
189262924e7717: William Harvey showed in 1628 that blood circulates: the heart pumps it through the arteries, it returns through the veins, and goes out again, in a loop. Before that, people believed the liver constantly produced blood. He measured the volume the heart pumped to show no other explanation fit.
0dcb71a6b9f944: Why do you think your pulse goes up when you exercise? Explain what your body needs at that moment.
0d8e8a3ddbb632: Measure your resting pulse for 30 seconds and multiply ×2. Measure it again after 1 minute of jumping jacks.
1573cfa2e853c9: In 1747, James Lind, a British navy physician, ran one of the first clinical trials: he gave different treatments to groups of sailors with scurvy and compared them. Those given lemons and oranges recovered. That disease is caused by a lack of vitamin C.
1f9542b65be41b: What food groups (fruits and vegetables, grains, proteins) does your favorite meal have? What's it missing?
1dda125d6cebea: Design a breakfast with at least three food groups and write it down.
117482c651b103: Santiago Ramón y Cajal observed with special stains that the brain is made of individual cells, neurons, separated by tiny gaps. For this theory he received the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 1906 (shared with Camillo Golgi). Today we know that sleeping well helps consolidate what you've learned.
129ee7fbafadba: Why do you think sleeping well helps you learn? How many hours do you usually sleep?
014063cf0afcb3: Turn off screens 30 minutes before bed tonight and note how you feel the next day.
090436d35a4d71: Florence Nightingale showed during the Crimean War (1853–1856) that washing hands and keeping hospitals clean saved far more lives than traditional care. She used statistics and charts to convince governments, and is considered the founder of modern nursing.
0014c6803088b7: Explain how a person should wash their hands before treating a wound, and why it matters.
18cc4d6db5504a: Practice washing your hands for 20 seconds and check what's in a basic first-aid kit at your home.
1b044ce9763cf6: Edward Jenner proved in 1796 that inoculating material from cowpox protected against human smallpox. The word "vaccine" comes from the Latin vacca (cow). Smallpox was declared eradicated in 1980 thanks to vaccination.
1484f45da76f6f: Why does a vaccine protect other people besides the one who gets it?
12b9311fa21dde: Check (or ask) which vaccines you're up to date on and when your next checkup is.
05d3d73122c29f: Hippocrates, in ancient Greece, argued that diseases have natural causes, not divine ones, and that you must observe the patient. The Hippocratic Oath, in its various versions, still inspires medical ethics today: help, respect the patient and keep professional confidentiality.
19711aa91822e2: Why is confidentiality between a doctor and their patient important?
03de7a7b891edb: Spend 10 minutes stretching and breathing slowly, and note how your mood changed.
1db2c2848f2f73: Every language is a new way of thinking.
073c781e26a39f: Ludwik Zamenhof created Esperanto in 1887 with the idea that a neutral, easy language would help people from different countries understand each other. Learning to greet someone in another language is the best way to start connecting with another culture.
0bc5f2ec7fc705: In how many languages do you know how to greet someone? Which would you like to learn first, and why?
11b46e8712487b: Learn to say "hello" and "thank you" in a language you don't speak and use it with someone today.
05ede9642ef16e: After the Norman conquest of England in 1066, French became the language of the court for centuries. That's why English has so many words of French and Latin origin alongside its Germanic roots. William Shakespeare popularized or coined hundreds of expressions still used today.
07fa876951b1e3: Name 5 objects in your room in English. Does any of them sound like the Spanish word?
14d140acc75b0e: Label 5 objects in your room in English and read them every time you pass by.
010e73a520872d: Ferdinand de Saussure argued that the linguistic sign joins a signifier (the sound or word) with a signified (the idea), and that the link is arbitrary — that's why each language names the same thing differently. And there are nearly untranslatable words, like saudade in Portuguese or sobremesa in Spanish.
0766d611d9a984: Find a word from another language that has no exact translation in your language. What idea does it express?
064d3bd03efc63: Write a sentence explaining an untranslatable word to someone who doesn't know it.
1322014254cfaf: Noam Chomsky proposed that human beings are born with a capacity for language: children learn to speak without formal lessons, just from being exposed to it. To learn another language as an adult, listening to it a lot helps a lot, just like children do.
01ed28c7a1a35a: Why do you think a language is learned better by hearing it often?
10e3d3d12605c6: Listen to a song in another language and note 3 words you recognize or want to look up.
0c2ef6354e8300: The Rosetta Stone, found in 1799, has the same text in hieroglyphic, demotic and Greek. Jean-François Champollion used it to decipher Egyptian hieroglyphs in 1822, after they had been forgotten for centuries.
0b2b0b59b1c713: Why do you think having the same text in three languages helped decipher one of them?
18d995b0c724ee: Write a sentence with 3 new words you've learned this week.
1866d9cfa53284: Don Quixote, by Miguel de Cervantes (1605), is one of the most translated works in history. Translating isn't swapping word for word: you have to carry over the humor, the rhythm and the meaning, which is why every translation is also an interpretation.
0bb8d96cac2dee: Do you think a joke can be translated without losing what makes it funny? Give an example.
0a376cc3302272: Watch a short video in another language with subtitles and write down a phrase you want to remember.
0ec9b25f6b4d0b: Sequoyah, a Cherokee craftsman, created a syllabary for writing the Cherokee language around 1821, without ever having learned to read another language. Within a few years, a large part of his people learned to read and write. It shows that every language deserves to be written and preserved.
1c32de92f95f8f: Why is it important to preserve languages spoken by few people?
1c945eecd39ec5: Introduce yourself out loud in the language you're studying: who you are, what you like, and what you want to learn.
1fe93975565cc2: Asking, experimenting and verifying: the scientific method in action.
057f2835e2ae4e: Galileo studied falling bodies and proposed that, without air resistance, everything falls with the same acceleration regardless of weight. Legend says he tested it from the Tower of Pisa, but that story is probably more legend than fact: his experiments used inclined planes.
0438b2b2716193: If you drop a sheet of paper and a rock, the rock lands first. Is it because of its weight or the air? How would you test it?
04c8f1e2f1000c: Drop a flat sheet of paper and the same sheet crumpled into a ball. Note what you see and why.
09e8bf0dad1565: Marie Curie discovered the elements polonium and radium, and coined the term "radioactivity." She's the only person with Nobel Prizes in two different sciences: Physics (1903, shared) and Chemistry (1911). She worked with dangerous materials without protection, which harmed her health.
1251b52bd4204f: What precautions matter when doing chemistry experiments at home?
1fb761818a53b2: Mix vinegar and baking soda in a large container (carefully, in an open space) and note what you observe.
1bf310f24c2de3: Charles Darwin proposed in On the Origin of Species (1859) that species change over time through natural selection: individuals with traits that help them survive and reproduce leave more offspring. His observations in the Galápagos Islands were key.
09cc872b61705f: Observe a living thing nearby (a plant, an insect). What trait of it helps it survive in its environment?
161b3e9d22023b: Watch a plant for 5 minutes and note 3 details you hadn't noticed before.
16298384d3fe39: Nicolaus Copernicus proposed in 1543 that Earth and the planets orbit the Sun (the heliocentric model), not the other way around. The Moon's phases depend on how much of its Sun-lit face we see as it orbits Earth — it's not Earth's shadow.
147c2ea55fae0e: Explain why the Moon changes shape over the course of the month.
11068d3a7d6eef: Look for the Moon tonight and note its phase; draw it.
199dc92ca6cd5f: Ibn al-Haytham, in his Book of Optics, explained that we see because light enters the eye, and argued for testing ideas with repeatable experiments. That's why he's considered a forerunner of the scientific method: observe, form a hypothesis, test it and review.
0ff114a2da01a5: Form a hypothesis about something everyday (for example, "ice melts faster with salt"). How would you test it?
0fb7332f9b9cc6: Write down your hypothesis, what you need to test it, and what result you expect.
147b502c209a5d: In 1859, Louis Pasteur used swan-neck flasks to prove that microbes don't appear "out of nowhere": they only grow if they reach the flask from the air. With this he disproved the theory of spontaneous generation and laid the groundwork for modern hygiene and vaccines.
15d9ba6ea7f363: Why is it important for an experiment to have a control group (a "no change" test) for comparison?
11f0b0e0259fc0: Do a mini-experiment: put bread in two bags, one sealed and one open. Watch it for a few days and take notes.
1a1aee8f4b4b9d: Rosalind Franklin obtained the famous "Photo 51" using X-rays, an image of DNA that was key to discovering its double-helix shape. Watson and Crick used it, and she didn't receive the recognition she deserved at the time. She died in 1958, before the 1962 Nobel Prize.
09ae99fc349f07: Why is it important to recognize the work of everyone who contributes to a discovery?
14d15b2b72bdb2: Write down what you learned from your experiment this week and what you'd do differently.
0139495507c2e0: Leonardo da Vinci filled thousands of notebook pages with drawings: anatomy, machines, plants, water. For him, drawing was a way of understanding the world: observing closely before creating. He also painted the Mona Lisa and The Last Supper.
0966db599cd2ad: What nearby object would you draw to understand it better? What details do you discover while drawing it?
11e9151e958ae8: Draw an object from your desk without lifting the pencil off the paper for a minute.
125584cf0235f8: Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz, in New Spain, was a poet, playwright and advocate for women's right to study. Her poem "Foolish men who accuse women without reason…" criticizes the double standard. She's one of the great figures of the Spanish Golden Age.
1d8de8e60f0d53: Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz
160513080167b0: Read a short poem out loud. What image, sound or feeling did it leave you with?
0709481b255b6e: Copy a line you like and write why you liked it.
09e8bc84dacb26: Vincent van Gogh used intense colors and thick brushstrokes to express emotion rather than copy reality, as in The Starry Night (1889). He painted hundreds of works in just a few years and sold very few in his lifetime; today they're among the most valued in the world.
171805faa250f7: What colors represent your mood today, and why?
1d322b50890ffa: Choose a 3-color palette for your mood and make a mini drawing with it.
11825311df3db0: Ludwig van Beethoven kept composing masterpieces even after going nearly deaf, like his Ninth Symphony (1824). Music is built from rhythm, melody and harmony; recognizing a song's pulse is the first step to understanding it.
172d355063babb: What song has been with you lately? What's its rhythm, and what feeling does it bring up?
0c940a5942beec: Clap out the beat of your favorite song and count how many beats each measure has.
13a00118e139f4: Gabriel García Márquez, Colombian and 1982 Nobel laureate in Literature, popularized magical realism: telling the extraordinary as if it were ordinary, as in One Hundred Years of Solitude (1967). He started his career as a journalist, where he learned to tell stories with precision.
1d50c648bbc853: Write the opening of a story where something extraordinary happens completely matter-of-factly.
1927362d715645: Write a 6-word story (yes, just 6) about a moment from your week.
095a824d73d752: Sophocles was one of the great authors of Greek theater. In Oedipus Rex (around 429 BC) the protagonist discovers the truth about himself. Theater brought the whole city together to think together about fate, justice and guilt.
19ab3b23263501: What scene from your life would you turn into a play? Who would the characters be?
037632f9f52049: Act out a scene from your life in 1 minute (with voice and gestures) in front of a mirror or someone else.
1820ac62ed6ca6: Frida Kahlo turned her personal experience, including pain and Mexican identity, into self-portraits full of symbols and color. She painted about 55 self-portraits and today is an icon of Latin American art.
10c0b459cdd329: What symbols would you include in a self-portrait that speaks to who you are?
1c61f0c17a943a: Share something you made this week with someone and tell them what you wanted to express.
1a1aad0cfeaeb2: Money, decisions, and how a society organizes itself.
19d7391900b7da: Adam Smith published The Wealth of Nations in 1776. He explained that division of labor (like in a pin factory, where each worker does one task) greatly increases production. He's considered the father of modern economics.
0dc373425187ab: What task at home or school gets done faster when the work is divided up?
05c1b9af1e5688: Write down everything you spent today and sort it into: need or want.
16c59f5fdd51d7: Alfred Marshall popularized the supply and demand graph in the late 19th century: the price of a good adjusts until what people want to buy matches what's being offered. If something is scarce and everyone wants it, the price goes up.
013198b430769e: Why do prices go up for things that are scarce and highly wanted (like tickets to a famous concert)?
09ac676d68d280: Pick a product you buy often and note whether its price changed in the last few months and why you think that happened.
1004ddd346ab36: John Maynard Keynes explained the "paradox of thrift": if everyone saves at the same time, consumption drops and the economy can slow down. Even so, saving is key at a personal level: a small goal with a deadline is easier to hit than a vague "I'll save more."
13b9fbd3cad654: Set a small savings goal (how much, and by when?) and explain how you'd achieve it.
0abd65c21ced18: Set aside a small amount today for your goal, even if it's symbolic.
1a6675a9db4c65: Montesquieu, in The Spirit of the Laws (1748), argued for the separation of powers: that whoever makes the laws, whoever applies them, and whoever judges should be different people, so no one holds absolute power. That idea inspired many modern constitutions.
04f3df3ce8df70: Name three rights you have as a student. Who should guarantee them?
0b77d787953253: Find out what rights your country's constitution protects and note two you didn't know about.
07c564dccc4c0f: Muhammad Yunus, an economist from Bangladesh, founded the Grameen Bank to give small loans (microcredit) to poor people that traditional banks ignored, especially women entrepreneurs. He received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2006 along with the bank.
11a466ddda4083: Imagine a product or service that solves a problem you or your community have. Who would use it?
18c40c5881325e: Write your idea in 5 lines: what problem it solves, for whom, and how much it would cost.
124a4dac32acaf: The Art of War, attributed to Sun Tzu (traditionally between the 6th and 5th centuries BC), teaches that the best victory is the one won without fighting: know your rival and yourself, and choose well when to act. His ideas are also applied today to business strategy.
162f8a67a40508: What would you do if your idea or project failed? Think of a plan B.
194f04c7d0bb29: Make a list of 3 risks in your idea from this week and a way to reduce each one.
06146ecd9d0d20: Elinor Ostrom studied how real communities take care of shared resources, like forests, water or fisheries, without anyone owning them. She showed they can do it with clear rules made by themselves. She was the first woman to win the Nobel Prize in Economics, in 2009.
07823c1f361748: What shared resource do you take care of with other people (the living room, the internet, a park)? What rules help it work?
19d456ecfa5bf2: Review your spending for the week and write down one decision you'll make for next week.
1b42bb827d5300: Thinking in steps and giving instructions to a computer.
00aed9bcd5e046: Donald Knuth wrote The Art of Computer Programming, a work that studies algorithms with mathematical rigor. An algorithm is a list of clear steps for solving a problem: a well-written recipe already is one.
0b165ade84e010: Write the steps for making tea (or your favorite food) clear enough that someone with no experience could follow them.
0a676640267a7d: Ask someone to follow your steps exactly. Did anything fail? Fix it.
1f5d65232ed3d5: Dennis Ritchie created the C language (1972) and worked on Unix. In programming, a variable is a "named box" that holds a piece of data, like age = 15, name = "Ana" or isStudent = true. Every piece of data has a type: number, text, true/false.
115ba0b84ef7c5: What value would you store in "age", "name" and "isStudent"? What type is each one?
03934185fb1497: Write down 5 variables about yourself (name, age, city, etc.) with their data type.
06de08d5fc5673: George Boole created an algebra in 1847 where the only values are true or false, with operations like AND, OR and NOT. It's the basis for conditionals in programming ("if it rains, I bring an umbrella; if not, I don't") and for digital circuits.
134382e8e7b686: Write an "if… then… else…" to decide what clothes to wear based on the weather.
12870bcdfbad69: Write 3 conditionals from your day (for example, "if I'm hungry, then…").
06c6c26043c468: Joseph Marie Jacquard created a loom controlled by punched cards in 1804: the holes indicated which threads to raise and lower, repeating complex patterns. That system inspired Babbage and, later, the first computers. A loop in programming repeats instructions several times.
016e59fe869331: What task do you repeat several times a day? How would you describe it as a loop ("repeat 5 times…")?
144c02223115f4: Write a loop in plain language for washing dishes or putting away your clothes.
0e7e7db04c9d91: Grace Hopper created one of the first compilers (1952), which translates near-English instructions into machine code. She's credited with popularizing the term "bug": in 1947, on the Harvard Mark II, a moth was found trapped in a relay. Debugging is finding and fixing errors.
1fbc61b11ce291: When a recipe goes wrong, how do you find which step failed? Apply the same idea to a program.
04642bc8140754: Read through one of your instructions or recipes step by step and try to find a hidden error.
19a45f86e93072: Brian Kernighan popularized the "hello, world" program in the 1978 C book: the simplest way to check that you can already write and run code. Almost every programmer starts with it in whatever language they're learning.
1cdb028012a937: Why do you think it's a good idea to start with a very simple program before making a complex one?
0e56aa906449f2: Write your first "hello, world" (for example, on a site like programiz.com or replit.com).
12ccd6ed990fbb: Linus Torvalds published the first version of Linux in 1991, an operating system anyone can read, modify and share (open source). Today it runs on most Internet servers and on Android. Sharing code lets thousands of people improve the same project.
1aeb9ed7aeb5b0: Explain what a program is to someone who knows nothing about computers, using an everyday example.
1fa0d4bc734809: Write down three programming concepts you learned this week and an example of each.
19b3685d4d4d8d: How we think, learn and communicate.
0adb8f558008c1: Paul Ekman studied facial expressions across cultures and proposed that there are basic emotions recognized all over the world: joy, sadness, fear, anger, surprise and disgust. Putting a precise name to what you feel helps you manage it better.
0c7cba1d5227c2: Name precisely how you feel right now. Is it anger, frustration, tiredness, anxiety? What caused it?
11430b17d6198a: Four times today, stop and write down in one word how you feel.
088187e21ad1eb: Daniel Kahneman, 2002 Nobel laureate in Economics, explained in Thinking, Fast and Slow that we make decisions using two modes: one fast and automatic, the other slow and reflective. The first is useful but falls into biases, like trusting too much in whatever comes to mind first.
0b5d892eb4b3f0: When did you decide quickly and got it wrong? What would have helped you think more slowly?
036f949ca2aee2: Before a decision today, count to 10 and ask yourself: "what information am I missing?"
02955478ffe5a2: Hermann Ebbinghaus measured in 1885 how much we forget over time: the forgetting curve shows we lose most of what we learned within a few days if we don't review it. Reviewing at intervals (spaced repetition) helps memories last longer.
15431e8d0a8790: How do you study? Do you review, or read everything the night before? What would you change?
0b90b26492777f: Pick something you learned a few days ago and explain it out loud without looking at your notes.
123d51c4004cde: Marshall Rosenberg developed nonviolent communication: expressing what you observe, what you feel, what you need and what you ask for, without accusing. Changing "you never listen to me" to "when you interrupt I feel ignored and I need you to let me finish" opens up dialogue.
1822e344e72fa4: Rephrase a complaint you have as a clear, respectful request.
1daddea876ea05: Today, use the formula "when… I feel… I need… could you…?" once with someone.
1732c7d76b1703: Marshall McLuhan said in 1964 that "the medium is the message": the way we receive information (TV, social media, a book) changes how we think, beyond just what it says. Asking who produced a piece of news and with what intent is part of reading media critically.
0521bf0e73cf55: Who produced the last news story or post you saw, and with what intent?
14e157faa0e6a5: Pick a news story and compare how two different outlets tell it.
1814479c7279b8: Carl Rogers proposed a person-centered approach to helping others, with three key attitudes: accepting without judging, being genuine, and listening with empathy. Really listening isn't waiting for the other person to finish so you can talk — it's trying to understand what they feel.
0457e1389c0f9a: How do you know when someone is really listening to you? What do they do?
06ee17a6933d02: Listen to someone for 5 minutes without interrupting or giving advice. When you're done, summarize what you understood.
0dc71c9921f9fb: Viktor Frankl, a psychiatrist and survivor of Nazi concentration camps, wrote Man's Search for Meaning (1946). He argued that even in extreme conditions we can choose our attitude, and that finding meaning helps us endure.
0036d3980e4814: What gives your day-to-day life meaning? What would you like to give it meaning?
13cc8a3c3eea9c: Write down three things that went well this week and why you're grateful for them.
